background:
Use case: background-extraction / historical-scene.
Produce a CLEAN ROOM BACKGROUND PLATE for an original Sherlock Holmes VGA point-and-click adventure. Reference 1 defines the approved illustrated Victorian style, colour direction, furnishings and character of the workshop. Reference 2 defines the production ROOM LAYOUT and modest furniture SCALE ONLY, NOT its crude geometry or flat style.
Scene: a clockmaker's Victorian workshop. Cold slate-blue sash window at left; faded olive plaster rear wall with three modest walnut/brass wall clocks; central sturdy workbench with clock gears, tools and burgundy cloth; a narrow very dark hidden passage on the right. Believable softly stylized perspective and finely grouped painted pixel shading inspired by early LucasArts Indiana Jones, Lost Files of Sherlock Holmes and Return of the Phantom. Painted and stylized yet naturalistic. Use reference1's medium detail, not photographic texture.
Strict image layout, described on the FINAL 320x200 source grid: rear wall spans x105..319 y24..139. Window x20..90 y32..117. Central workbench top x116..219 y105..119, legs extend to y145. Three modest wall clocks centered roughly (138,59), (171,48), (216,46), faces 12 to 18 source pixels diameter. All hands at3:17. Keep a thin shelf/tool rail below them. A simple closed dark timber door with visible brass sliding bolt occupies far right strip x290..319 y48..146. DARK GAP for removable grandfather case occupies x257..282 y56..149, a narrow shadowed opening with a few blue-gray descending stair edges at the bottom; it will be COVERED by a separate moving prop in game. Do not draw any grandfather clock, clock cabinet, clock hood, pendulum or door over this gap. The perspective floor band spans y145..199, wider across bottom, unobstructed across center so a60px-tall actor can walk. Keep lower-left corner as EMPTY FLOOR ready for a separately layered near table. No foreground furniture.
Production exclusions essential: NO PEOPLE, NO HOLMES, NO foreground ledger table, NO lantern or oil lamp (leave bare worktop under it around190,111), NO brass filings on floor, NO scratches clue. Paint underlying wall/workbench/floor fully in areas vacated by these objects. Use a soft amber lit area on workbench and local rear wall as ambient painted illumination, but no painted duplicate light source.
Materials and palette: olive-gray plaster, walnut and oak, burgundy cloth accents, muted amber highlights, cool slate blue window. Moderate light/dark contrast and selective medium-size pixel clusters. Avoid photographic grain, decorative noise, bloom and glossy texture. Do not distort walls or bow boards. This will be reduced to320x200 and ONE shared64-colour palette so details must be simple and deliberate, floor quiet not noisy. Visibly illustrated pixel adventure art, not a photo, not a 3D render, not vector illustration.
Output one full-frame4:3 landscape image. No UI, labels, border, captions, characters, frames, letterboxing.
holmes:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: production character animation sprite sheet on TRUE TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND.
Create exactly 21 separate full-body Sherlock Holmes sprites, arranged in a precise GRID OF 7 COLUMNS AND 3 ROWS, equal cells, generous transparent gutters, no overlap, no text or grid lines. Output a square sheet. All figures are the SAME character, same costume, same scale, same floor baseline within their cell.
Use the attached Sherlock workshop as character and colour reference only. Holmes has natural slender ADULT body proportions (7 to7.5 heads tall), charcoal Victorian frock coat to above knees, burgundy waistcoat, cream collar, dark trousers, modest olive-brown deerstalker hat and a SMALL curved pipe held in his lips. Keep his face angular but not exaggerated. Pixel-adventure illustration, early1990s VGA detail, no photo texture, readable when each full figure is60 pixels tall. Around12–16 colours within existing olive/walnut/burgundy/slate/skin tones; no bright white outfit. Crisp compact shading.
GRID EXACTLY:
ROW1: ALL SEVEN FIGURES IN STRICT RIGHT-FACING SIDE PROFILE (east). Column1 STANDING STILL arms relaxed. Columns2–7 a smooth six-pose WALK CYCLE: left leg forward/right leg back contact; weight down with left planted; right leg passes under body; right leg forward/left leg back contact; weight down with right planted; left leg passes under body. Counter-swing arms naturally, modest stride, coat tails move subtly. Foot placement and limb poses MUST vary visibly. Pipe points to right, hat fixed to head. Do not change facing or show3/4 in row1.
ROW2: ALL SEVEN FIGURES FACING VIEWER (south). Column1 STANDING. Columns2–7 same six cycle phases WALKING TOWARD VIEWER, left/right feet alternate foreshortening and arm swing, head stays facing viewer. Clearly front of face, waistcoat and coat lapels visible.
ROW3: ALL SEVEN FIGURES FACING AWAY (north). Column1 STANDING. Columns2–7 six cycle phases WALKING AWAY, opposite steps and swing, back of hat/head and back of frock coat, NO face or shirtfront. Feet alternate, coat seam visible.
Keep all body proportions consistent; no chibi head, no giant shoes, no cape, no hands gripping lapels during walking. Each standing pose and6walk poses occupy the SAME HEIGHT and canvas scale; a slight walking bob is allowed. Both feet fit within each cell. No floor, shadows, scenery, labels, swatches, weapons, smoke, bounding boxes or additional poses. REAL alpha transparency, not a checkerboard drawing. Each figure must be cleanly isolated so the grid can be sliced into sprites.
props:

Match the attached workshop's restrained Victorian painted pixel-art look and its olive/walnut/burgundy/slate/amber palette. This is a sheet of EXACTLY THREE ISOLATED OBJECTS with generous separation, left to right, NO environment.
LEFT THIRD: a closed tall-case walnut grandfather clock, full object with no crop. Straight nearly front-facing view, modest decorative hood and brass clock face hands at3:17, long glass panel showing brass pendulum, sturdy rectangular base. The whole case should have a clear narrow rectilinear silhouette, cabinet height about3.1 times its width. No floor shadow extending outside the base. No wall. Closed only, one clock.
MIDDLE THIRD: a near foreground dark walnut desk/table viewed from slightly above, receding moderately to upper-right, with an open cream ledger, simple small inkpot and a dark burgundy blotter. Broad tabletop, near edge and two visible legs, solid modest joinery. This is a cutout which will enter from LOWER LEFT of a320x200 room. Table width about1.6times its visible height. Draw its whole silhouette so we may deliberately crop at screen edges. Nothing behind it, no chair, no floor.
RIGHT THIRD: one small Victorian oil lantern with a restrained brass base, clear simple chimney/metal frame and a warm flame. Front-facing slight3/4 view, whole lantern visible with a tiny handle, isolated. Height about1.8times width. No light halo outside the silhouette, NO soft glow/translucency on transparent background: shading and flame confined inside the object.
All three objects have binary-looking clean edges, medium pixel clusters and simple shading so they remain readable at small resolution; no intricate photographic grain, no rendered3D reflections, no labels, no text, no title, no checkerboard drawing, no colour swatches or decorations. All background and gaps between objects truly transparent. No shadows outside object contours, do not overlap objects. Draw at a scale suitable for clean downsampling to small palette sprites.
